title: Selling and shops
summary: How to sell items, what each shopkeeper buys and sells, and the prices.

s.x: Skyhaven's shopkeepers buy what you gather and sell what you need to keep going. This page explains how selling and buying work, what each keeper takes, and what is on every shelf. Prices are in coins unless a column says otherwise.
There are three ways to sell. They all pay the
same price per item
Right-click a keeper who buys things. The shop screen has a
sell panel
on the right that lists what you carry that this keeper wants.
Click an item to sell
all
of it.
Click
Sell all
to sell everything this keeper wants.
Each keeper only buys their own trade. Mabel will not buy ore, and Brannoc will not buy wheat.
After you sell, a
Buy back
button appears. It returns your last sale at that keeper for the same coins, as long as your inventory has room and you can pay.
These work anywhere, with no keeper, at the same prices.

rows.x: Sells the stack in your hand
Sells every stack of the item in your hand
Sells everything in your inventory and hotbar that has a price
Shows the price of the item in your hand, and of the whole stack

s.x: Armour you wear and your offhand are never sold. Backpack contents are not touched either.
/sell inventory
sells
everything
with a price, including rare finds. A Heartstone sells for 15,000 and a Prism Fragment for 1,500, but both are worth more as crafting ingredients. A shopkeeper's
Sell all
button skips them, because no keeper lists them. Use
/worth
first if you are unsure.
If an item has no price, NPCs will not buy it. Most SkyRPG weapons, armour, tools and accessories have none, so there is no way to turn them back into coins.
Click an offer to buy one.
Shift-click
buys a full stack, and
right-click
lets you pick a number: type it, use the arrow keys, or choose 1, 8, 16, 32 or 64, then press
Enter
. You can buy at most a full inventory's worth in one go.
Offers you cannot afford show how many coins you are short.
Offers that need a skill level you do not have show "Needs Mining 10" in red.
Some offers cost
items
instead of coins, such as Glimmer Crystals at Tamsin or Dew Vials at Mabel. The cost shows as icons with counts, red where you are short. The items are taken from your inventory.
If your inventory is nearly full, you buy as many as fit.
Bought SkyRPG items come with their proper name, rarity and stats.
Stay within 10 blocks of the keeper. If you walk further away the shop refuses the trade.

s.x: The Builder, the Florist and the Curio Dealer do not buy anything.
Marina's shop lists nautilus shells among the things she wants, but they have no sell price, so she will not pay for them.
No keeper lists these, so the only way to turn them into coins is
/sell
. Most are rare finds, boss drops and dungeon trophies, and are better kept for crafting.
The six danger-region sigils sell for 3,000 each. The region bosses' trophies sell for 14,000 to 30,000. Region essences sell for 60.
Skyiron, Duskquartz and Emberite blocks sell for 90, 126 and 216 each, nine times the ingot or shard price. Tamsin does not list them, so they also need
/sell

Coins buy the basic gear. Level-gated offers use the trade's own currency: Glimmer Crystals, Dew Vials, Heartwood Bundles, Tidescales and Valor Marks. A cost of "12 Dewdrops" means 12 of that item from your inventory, not coins.
Do not sell raw materials you will craft with. Skyiron, Emberite and Lumenite are worth far more as gear at the Artisan Bench. See
Crafting
Contracts usually pay more than the same goods sold. See
Contracts
Glimmer, Dew, Heartwood and Tidescales sell for very little but buy a lot from their Master. Keep them to spend.
